one_month_reasoning: Two scheduled events fall in the window, both on 2026-10-15: Alcoa's Q3 2026 results (after the close) and South32's shareholder vote on selling its aluminium assets to Alcoa. Q3 guidance from July was only modestly sequential (tariff cost -$10M, alumina +$10M, op. tax $80-90M), but the realized-price inputs moved against Alcoa: the Midwest premium fell from a record ~$1.19/lb in June to ~$0.95-1.09/lb after the Aug 20 Canada tariff-cut headlines, LME was roughly flat at ~$3,200-3,300/t, and alumina sits near $350-370/t FOB WA in a growing surplus. So Q3 should be well below Q2's $901M adjusted EBITDA; sell-side targets have already been cut (Wells Fargo $71->$60 on Sep 18) and the stock is down ~20% in September with peers (CENX) falling too, so much of that is likely priced in. The South32 vote is likely to pass (South32 shares rose on the deal), which removes one uncertainty but locks in the leverage. Other in-window swing factors: post-Golden-Week Chinese restocking, any revival of US-Canada tariff talks (negative for the Midwest premium), Gulf/Hormuz headlines. Net: no directional edge, slight downside skew from momentum offset by cheapness; I center the distribution at ~$41.8 with monthly sigma ~16.5% (56%/3.5 plus a bit for earnings).

fair_value.method: Blend of 2027E P/E ($4.90 x 9x = $44.1, weight 0.45), 2027E EV/EBITDA ($2.5B x 5.0x less ~$0.9B net debt over 264M shares = $44.0, weight 0.45) and the sell-side average target ($63, weight 0.10) = ~$46. The South32 deal (closing 1H27, ~$4.1B for EBITDA-producing assets at roughly the same multiple) is treated as value-neutral per share.

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus $5.72 cut ~15%: EGA's Al Taweelah (~1.6 Mtpa) targets full output by Q1 2027, removing the Gulf supply shock that lifted LME; Midwest premium is already off its June record on Canada tariff talk and could fall further; alumina in surplus at ~$350-370/t so the Alumina segment stays near breakeven (Q2 -$96M).

Commodity producer on elevated-price earnings deserves a below-market multiple; Q2 annualized adj EPS $8.48 vs $42 price = ~5x run-rate and consensus 2027 $5.72 = 7.3x, market clearly capitalizing peak earnings; 9x on haircut normalized-ish EPS is a mid-cycle multiple for AA.

inputs_detail.derivation: Q2 run-rate ~$3.6B; assume blended realized aluminum price falls ~$650-750/t (LME ~$2,900 as Gulf supply returns; Midwest premium ~$0.80/lb vs ~$1.0-1.19/lb) on ~2.6-2.7 Mt shipments (-~$1.8B), partly offset by lower Section 232 tariff costs and alumina cost relief; alumina segment ~breakeven at $350-370/t API.

At $42 AA trades ~3.3x Q2 run-rate EBITDA (EV ~$12B); peer CENX derated in parallel (from ~$70 to ~$36), showing the market applies low multiples to elevated aluminum earnings; 5x on a normalized 2027 EBITDA is a conservative mid-cycle multiple.

inputs_detail.derivation: Treated as value-neutral per share: adds debt and ~17M shares but also Worsley, Hillside, Alumar/MRN EBITDA; closes 1H 2027.
Small weight only as cross-check; targets lag and are being cut (Wells Fargo $71->$60).

bear.story: Gulf smelters (EGA Q1 2027) fully back and China at record output push LME to ~$2,500-2,700; a US-Canada deal halves the Section 232 rate and the Midwest premium falls toward $0.50-0.60/lb; alumina stays in surplus; Alcoa carries ~$3B of new debt into the South32 close with lower prices; EBITDA ~$1.6-1.8B, 4.5-5x.

base.story: LME drifts to ~$2,900, Midwest premium ~$0.75-0.85/lb as tariffs stay at 50% but Gulf supply returns; 2027 EBITDA ~$2.5B, deal closes 1H27 roughly neutral; stock re-rates modestly from depressed multiple to ~9x EPS / 5x EBITDA.

bull.story: Gulf restoration slips or new disruption, US tariffs persist with Canada talks dead (Section 338 escalation), Midwest premium stays >$1/lb and LME >$3,200; alumina recovers on Chinese cuts; 2027 EBITDA $3.5B+ and deal synergies (~$900M NPV) visible; stock retraces toward sell-side highs ($76-80).

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$28 (one-third under today and below the 52-week low of $31.45) the market would be discounting EBITDA well under $2B, i.e. LME back to ~$2,500 plus a collapsed Midwest premium, or financing/integration trouble on the South32 deal. That would mean the normalization I assume has overshot into a real downcycle rather than ordinary volatility.

Speed of Gulf supply recovery (EGA, Alba, Qatalum) and LME response

reasoning: AA is a pure play on aluminum and alumina prices, so I read it through the chain. The 2026 spike (Iranian strikes on Gulf smelters, Hormuz logistics, Midwest premium record ~$1.19/lb, Q2 realized $4,752/t, Q2 adj EBITDA $901M) drove AA to $84 in early June; since then the stock halved, in parallel with Century Aluminum (~$70 to ~$36), which says the driver is sector-wide de-rating rather than AA-specific news, though the South32 deal (bridge financing, ~17M new shares) and a Q2 alumina miss added to it. Chain evidence points to normalization ahead: EGA targets full Al Taweelah output by Q1 2027, LME stocks/ spreads eased in September, the Midwest premium fell on Canada tariff-cut headlines (deal later collapsed, keeping tariffs at 50% for now), alumina is in widening surplus at ~$355-369/t. On the other hand primary ingot inventories are tight, US demand is solid per Century/Kaiser, and AA trades ~5x run-rate EPS and ~3.3x run-rate EBITDA. My normalized 2027 view (EPS ~$4.90, EBITDA ~$2.5B) gives ~$44 on mid-cycle multiples, ~$46 including a small weight to sell-side targets. Scenarios 27/46/68 at 25/50/25 give a mean ~$47; I set the 12m distribution as lognormal with median ~$44.5 and sigma 0.48 (a bit under the 56% realized vol, since vol was inflated by the spike-and-crash). One-month: centered at ~$41.8 with sigma ~16.5% given Oct 15 earnings and the South32 vote. Research was limited to ~20 queries; some figures (Midwest premium mid-September ~$1.09/lb) come from search snippets and conflict with other sources, so I used a range.
